page: Microsoft Azure E112ibs_v5 is an isolated, memory-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor. It features 112 vCPUs mapped to 56 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 6.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on external block storage with Premium Storage capabilities.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing and memory subsystem performance. The server achieves top-tier results in cryptographic operations, specifically the PassMark CPU encryption test, aided by hardware-accelerated instructions like AES and VAES. Multi-threaded tasks, such as software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and bzip3 decompression, fall into the top 25% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block transfers reaching 5839.55 GB/sec and uncached large block writes at 138.63 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core performance and LLM inference tasks for both small and medium models register in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E112ibs_v5 offers high resource density and dedicated compute allocation within an isolated environment, making it suitable for enterprise workloads requiring strict tenant isolation. The lack of local storage represents a trade-off, shifting storage performance dependencies entirely to external premium block storage. This configuration is highly suited for large-scale database operations, high-throughput static web serving, memory-intensive data processing, and multi-threaded enterprise applications.
